    Secrets and fear are the tradestuff of the Golden Dawn, and for this reason I will not give any of the names of members of the Golden Dawn in this chronicle. category: 🚢 Week two, The Tir Na Nog
content: My time in the Golden Dawn began with a simple message I received while tracking the origin of an amulet of theirs that I found on a werewolf that had marked the Tir Na Nog a week before our departure. They promised knowledge and power, and told me they had many Uru members. The day before the summoner attacked the Tir Na Nog, I was told the Golden Dawn would create a distraction that would allow me to place a box in the ship, a small lead box that the Golden Dawn had couriered to me and that I had been instructed not to open or examine. The summoner breached the magical defenses of the Tir Na Nog in his attack, allowing multiple boxes to be taken aboard without raising any magical alarms. This, to the best of my knowledge, was the true purpose behind that attack on the Tir Na Nog. No members of the Golden Dawn knew of the details of the attack before it occurred, we were only told that we would be provided a distraction. All of us, however, are guilty of going through with the mission in spite of the body count that 'distraction' entailed.

category: 🚢 Week two, The Tir Na Nog
content: The next day, we were inducted into the Golden Dawn, and entered the foreboding mansion on Tottenham court. We were told that the mansion itself would be used to attack the Tir Na Nog, and that we were to assist in the Tir Na Nog's defense. Some hours before the mansion's attack, we were instructed to burn down Generous Jack's shop. I arrived at the scene to find Jack's shop already burning and watched as Jack fled from his shop and into the Thames. I attempted to retrieve his body to no avail. Others attempted the same later that night, again to no avail.

category: 🚢 Week two, The Tir Na Nog
content: That quiet ended on the day the infernal contract was discovered. We were instructed to get Castor to sign it, and so I took it upon myself to go to Copper and let him know that he had an infernal contract. I did so by seeking the aid of Sir Wynne to translate, and when I saw that they intended to get Castor to sign it, I attempted to distance both myself and the Golden Dawn from the act by attacking Sir Wynne's character in a heavy-handed fashion. I then observed Castor and Copper discussing the matter in vague terms, until Fyr pulled Castor away, presumably to make things considerably less vague and to convince Castor to sign the contract. Seeing my part in this finished, I instructed another Golden Dawn member to make sure the deal was consummated while I waited in the Golden Dawn's chambers. Eventually, all but Rah arrived--the Golden Dawn member I had instructed to see the deal consummated arrived fuming. The contract had not been signed. Rah was forcibly teleported into the chambers and we were informed that he had given the names of most of our order to Amara and Castor. A vote was held, and Rah is executed by Power Word Kill. One who voted for his death was so overwhelmed by the events that their memory was struck as a mercy.

category: 🚢 Week two, The Tir Na Nog
content: We were instructed to silence Castor and Amara. One of our order requested scrolls of modify memory, that we might do it without violence. But we lacked members available to cast the scrolls. I returned Rah to his bed, and then I told Amara that Rah wishes to speak with her in room 2. Once she arrived, I cornered her and explained that she and Castor would be in great danger so long as they knew the names of the members of the Golden Dawn, that we could protect Castor from harm by removing his knowledge of the names, but that there remained a danger that the memories will returned with a simple casting of lesser restoration. The scheme only worked as long as there was somebody we could trust willing to monitor him and make sure that either the memories never return or that they are erased each time that they return. Amara would need to be that somebody we could trust. She reluctantly agreed, and we went into Castor's room. She cast modify memory, and I went through his things until I found his journal. I ripped out the last few pages.
